right_execution_tier.instructions: Across the integration, persistence, API/HTTP, and end-to-end test layers alongside the production code, are behaviors tested at the right execution tier—with pure domain logic covered directly in fast unit tests and heavyweight integration layers kept to their proper concerns?

criteria.pass: When production code contains substantial pure domain logic, policy rules, state transitions, or validation alongside an application, HTTP, database, or browser boundary, pure logic is covered directly in fast unit tests (not exclusively via heavyweight integration tests), transport/binding slices or persistence tests own their respective concerns, and high-level API or end-to-end tests stay thin vertical slices without mixing in unit-level direct calls or raw database constraint tests. Pure browser/UI end-to-end tasks with no separate backend or database service pass when pure client-side logic is minimal or sensibly separated.
criteria.fail: Production code contains substantial pure domain logic, policy rules, state transitions, or validation alongside an application/HTTP/database boundary, yet the test suite relies exclusively on heavyweight full-stack, HTTP, database, or browser integration tests with no direct unit tests for pure logic; OR pure logic tests needlessly boot a full application context, server, or database; OR a high-level API/E2E test class mixes in unit-level direct domain calls or raw database constraint tests.

integration_cohesive_scope.instructions: Within integration, persistence, API/HTTP, and end-to-end test layers, does each test cover either one focused contract check or one coherent user journey/lifecycle transition with a clear purpose rather than a sprawling kitchen-sink script?

criteria.pass: Each integration, persistence, API/HTTP, or end-to-end test has a clear, focused scope—verifying either one contract check or one coherent user journey or lifecycle transition (brief setup calls needed to reach the starting state are fine), with larger suites organized cleanly by capability.
criteria.fail: One or more integration, persistence, API/HTTP, or end-to-end tests act as sprawling kitchen-sink scripts that chain unrelated endpoints, independent workflows, and multiple unrelated error or validation rejections into a single mega-test.

shared_fixtures_no_raw_db_in_api.instructions: Do integration, API/HTTP, and end-to-end tests keep setup skimmable with shared fixtures/helpers and keep high-level API/E2E test bodies completely free of inline raw database queries or mutations?

criteria.pass: Shared fixture builders or client/actor helpers keep integration test bodies skimmable without copy-pasting private entity-creation helpers or hardcoded magic IDs across sibling test files. High-level API/HTTP and end-to-end test method bodies contain no inline raw database queries or mutations (a clean-slate reset in a setup/teardown hook is acceptable, and direct database queries belong in dedicated persistence tests or shared persistence fixtures). Suites with no database pass when setup helpers stay concise and shared rather than copy-pasted across sibling files.
criteria.fail: High-level API/HTTP or end-to-end test bodies contain inline raw database queries or mutations (such as direct SQL/table reads, inserts, updates, or row-count queries) instead of using public boundaries or dedicated persistence tests; OR sibling integration test files copy-paste private entity-creation/auth-setup helpers or hardcoded magic IDs instead of sharing them; OR repetitive low-level request/setup boilerplate obscures test intent.

real_internal_wiring.instructions: Do integration, API/HTTP, and end-to-end tests exercise real internal application wiring rather than mocking or spying on internal services or repositories inside a full-stack test context?

criteria.pass: Integration, persistence, API/HTTP, and end-to-end tests exercise real internal application wiring across real internal services, handlers, and repositories rather than replacing internal components with mocks or spies inside a full-stack test context. Faking or stubbing only external third-party boundaries (such as email gateways, payment providers, or external identity providers) is acceptable.
criteria.fail: Full-stack integration, API/HTTP, or end-to-end tests mock or spy on internal application services, domain collaborators, or internal repositories instead of exercising real internal wiring.
